sections.h2: Where is Lake Charles and what is around it?
sections.html:
Lake Charles is the parish seat of Calcasieu Parish in southwest Louisiana, on the shore of Lake Charles, Prien Lake and the Calcasieu River, about 30 miles from the Gulf of Mexico. It is the fifth most populous city in the state, with 84,872 residents at the 2020 census.

The ground is a level plain at roughly 13 feet above sea level. Contraband Bayou, Henderson Bayou and English Bayou run through town, and the Calcasieu Ship Channel borders it and carries ocean-going vessels up from the Gulf. The city has about 45 square miles of area, and a little over 6 percent of that is water. The region is often called the Lake Area, and the metropolitan area had about 240,000 people in 2023.

sections.h2: How did Lake Charles get its name and its growth pattern?
sections.html:
The town was incorporated in 1861 as Charleston, after early settler Charles Sallier, and became the City of Lake Charles in 1867. Calcasieu Parish moved its seat here in 1852 and the log courthouse was carried to the town by ox cart.

A great fire in April 1910 destroyed the courthouse and much of downtown, and the present courthouse was finished in 1912. Petrochemical refineries arrived during and after World War II, and the city grew to roughly 75,000 people by the early 1980s. Then a local recession followed, and the population stagnated near 70,000 for decades before the 2020 census count of 84,872. In 1985 the city was picked as a possible Navy strategic homeport, but the base was closed before it was finished.

sections.h2: What did the hurricanes do to Lake Charles housing?
sections.html:
Lake Charles was heavily damaged by Hurricane Rita in 2005 and then hit by Hurricane Laura on August 26 and 27, 2020 and Hurricane Delta on October 9, 2020. Laura was a Category 4 storm with one-minute sustained winds of 150 miles per hour, and the National Weather Service called the storm surge unsurvivable.

A gust of 133 miles per hour was recorded at Lake Charles Regional Airport, and the city also saw an EF2 tornado on October 27, 2021 and an EF1 tornado on May 13, 2024. Many local houses were damaged more than once. A seller today may own a house with a patched roof, a partial rebuild or a tarp that never became a full repair.

  • Gather insurance claim letters and payment records for each storm.
  • Keep contractor invoices, permits and final inspection papers.
  • Note any work that was started and not finished.
  • List what you know about mold, water intrusion or past gutting.

These records answer the first questions a buyer will ask. A house with partial repairs and no paperwork is harder to sell on the open market, and it is a common reason owners look for a buyer who will take it as it stands.

sections.h2: What does the Lake Charles climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Lake Charles is tied with Port Arthur, Texas, and Astoria, Oregon, as the most humid city in the contiguous United States, according to Wikipedia, with average relative humidity of about 90 percent in the morning and 72 percent in the afternoon.

Annual precipitation averages about 57 to 60 inches, and rain falls on about 108 days a year. Summer afternoons reach the low 90s. Humidity like that is hard on roofing, wood trim, attic insulation and air conditioning, and it feeds mold in any house that sat closed up after storm damage. The record low is 3 degrees, so pipe wraps are not an optional extra in a cold snap.

sections.h2: How does the assessor treat storm damage and homestead in Calcasieu Parish?
sections.html:
The Calcasieu Parish Assessor says it reduced values on structures throughout the parish for 2020 after Hurricanes Laura and Delta, and it provides a homestead continuation form for owners whose homes were damaged or destroyed by those storms or by flood.

The standard homestead exemption covers the first $7,500 of assessed value on an owner-occupied home, and the owner must sign for it in person at the assessor's office. Residential improvements and land are assessed at 10 percent of fair market value, and commercial property at 15 percent. More than 70 taxing districts, among them the School Board, Police Jury and fire protection districts, set the millage, so the bill depends on where the house sits.

The assessor's own example shows how the math runs: a $100,000 home is assessed at $10,000, and with homestead the parish part is figured on $2,500.

sections.h2: What happens if property tax goes unpaid before a Lake Charles sale?
sections.html:
Louisiana taxes are due by December 31, and the following day they are delinquent. Under R.S. 47:2127, interest runs at one percent per month, and a five percent penalty is added if the tax lien goes to a lien auction.

The assessor also warns that a missing tax notice does not excuse the owner, who is still responsible for confirming that the taxes were paid. If a house sat empty after a storm and the notices went to an old address, call the Calcasieu Parish Sheriff, who collects the tax, and ask what is owed before you set a closing date. Back taxes can be paid from proceeds at closing, though the amount is cleaner if you know it in advance.

sections.h2: How is a Lake Charles house sold under Louisiana law?
sections.html:
The sale is made by a written act, either authentic or under private signature, and it only counts against outside parties once it is filed for registry in the parish where the property sits (Civil Code art. 1839). For Lake Charles that is Calcasieu Parish.

The seller also owes the buyer a disclosure form by the time of the offer. R.S. 9:3198 allows you to mark facts as unknown, and it protects you if an error was not willful. A late form lets the buyer cancel within 72 hours. Given the history above, list storm damage and repairs on the form as accurately as you can.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers and what do they mean for sellers?
sections.html:
The Calcasieu Parish School System employs about 5,000 people, and L'Auberge Casino Resort comes second with about 2,400, according to Wikipedia. Turner Industries, Westlake Chemical and Citgo each employ over 1,000.

Other companies named there are PPG, Phillips 66, Sasol and Grace, and AAR Corp services airplanes at Chennault International Airport, where a Northrop Grumman facility also operates. The Lake Charles LNG terminal lies southwest of the city. Lake Charles has Louisiana's largest casino market, with L'Auberge, Golden Nugget and Horseshoe in nearby Westlake. McNeese State University, founded in 1939 with more than 8,500 students, and SOWELA Technical Community College add steady demand.

sections.h2: How do I get around Lake Charles?
sections.html:
Interstate 10 runs through the city and links Houston to the west with New Orleans to the east, and Interstate 210 loops through the south. U.S. 90 runs parallel to I-10, U.S. 171 goes north toward DeRidder and Shreveport, and Highway 165 runs northeast to Alexandria.

Lake Charles Regional Airport has commercial flights to Houston and Dallas, and the Port of Lake Charles is the 13th busiest seaport in the United States. The Calcasieu River Bridge on I-10 carries about 50,000 vehicles a day, and Lake Charles Transit runs five bus routes. Houses within a short drive of I-10 or I-210 are easy to show to commuters.

faqs.q: Did Hurricane Laura change property taxes in Calcasieu Parish?
faqs.a: The assessor reduced values on structures parish-wide for 2020 after Laura and Delta and offers a disaster homestead continuation form. Call 337-721-3000 for your own parcel.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lake Charles house with unrepaired storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Disclose the damage on the Louisiana form, share any claim and contractor papers you have, and expect buyers to price in the remaining work.

faqs.q: What interest applies to late Louisiana property tax?
faqs.a: One percent per month from the day after the due date, under R.S. 47:2127, plus a five percent penalty if the lien is offered at auction.

faqs.q: Who sets millage rates in Calcasieu Parish?
faqs.a: The more than 70 taxing districts, including the School Board and Police Jury, set rates. The assessor values property but does not set the rate.

faqs.q: Does the buyer get my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The new owner has to sign for homestead in person at the Calcasieu Parish Assessor's office.
Very. Wikipedia reports it ties for the most humid city in the contiguous United States, with morning relative humidity near 90 percent.
